The crew that keeps Rager flyable ✈️🌲

Eight volunteers pitched in this November at Rager Guard Station Airstrip in Central Oregon’s Ochoco National Forest. Some flew in aboard five aircraft. Others drove two and a half hours, hauling their own mowing and grading equipment.

They cut back brush, mowed and leveled the 2,800-foot gravel strip, repainted runway markers and put up new signs. They even repaired a weathered picnic table.

A backcountry strip takes work to keep usable. Here’s to the Recreational Aviation Foundation volunteers who showed up with the tools to do it.
